result.executive_summary: Northwind Semiconductors reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.2 billion, up 31% year over year, with data center accelerators growing 44% and contributing 70% of revenue. videos.summary: Northwind Semiconductors reported record Q3 FY2026 revenue of $4.2 billion, an increase of 31% year-over-year, driven by 44% growth in its data center accelerator business which now accounts for 70% of total revenue. Diluted earnings per share reached $1.12 with operating income of $1.3 billion, while gross margin declined 120 basis points sequentially to 61.5% due to elevated packaging costs. For Q4 FY2026, management guided revenue between $4.0 billion and $4.2 billion and gross margins around 60%, incorporating an estimated $300 million negative impact from new export license restrictions. Management announced a new $1.0 billion share repurchase program while noting customer concentration risks, with the top cloud customer generating 22% of revenue.

transcript_preview.speaker: Operator
transcript_preview.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to the Northwind Semiconductors third quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call. Today's call contains forward-looking statements, and actual results may differ materially. I will now hand the call over to our Chief Executive Officer, Dana Reyes.

transcript_preview.speaker: Dana Reyes (CEO)
transcript_preview.text: Thank you, and good afternoon everyone. Northwind delivered record revenue of $4.2 billion this quarter, up 31% from a year ago, driven by demand for our data center accelerators. Data center revenue grew 44% and now represents 70% of our business. At the same time, I want to be transparent about two headwinds. First, new export license requirements for advanced chips shipping to certain regions will reduce our fourth-quarter revenue by an estimated $300 million. Second, our largest cloud customer accounted for 22% of revenue, so our concentration remains high.

transcript_preview.speaker: Marcus Lin (CFO)
transcript_preview.text: Thanks, Dana. Gross margin was 61.5%, down 1.2 points sequentially, mainly because of higher packaging costs. Operating income was $1.3 billion. We ended the quarter with $5.8 billion in cash and $2.1 billion of long-term debt.

transcript_preview.speaker: Marcus Lin (CFO)
transcript_preview.text: For the fourth quarter, we expect revenue of $4.0 to $4.2 billion, which includes the impact of the export restrictions, and gross margin of approximately 60%. We are also announcing a new $1 billion share repurchase program.

transcript_preview.speaker: Priya (Analyst)
transcript_preview.text: Thanks for taking my question. Can you quantify how much of the guidance reduction is temporary and whether you can redirect that supply to other customers?

transcript_preview.speaker: Dana Reyes (CEO)
transcript_preview.text: Great question, Priya. We believe part of the impact is temporary while licenses are reviewed, and we are already in conversations to reallocate supply. However, we are being cautious in our guidance until we have more clarity.
